analysis.title: Nordic Alert: Anthropic's IPO beats records
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell for a fifth consecutive day after renewed declines in Nvidia. The Nasdaq rose against the tide ahead of Anthropic's market debut.

Anthropic's IPO had no trouble finding buyers. It broke SpaceX's record as the largest IPO ever and values the company at about 1500 billion USD. The report describes the deal as a test of the market's continued interest in AI.
Oil traded steadily overnight at 92 USD/barrel after New York Times reports that President Trump is considering new attacks on Iran together with Israel.
US 10-year yields rose by a few basis points on the Fed minutes but were otherwise stable. The market continues to price just over three more Fed hikes.

The October FOMC minutes showed most members supported holding rates unchanged and that almost all expected further tightening. A couple of members discussed a larger hike if inflation data came in unfavorably.

Waller repeated his call for a 50 basis point hike in December on CNBC. He said the Fed could settle for 25 basis points if it clearly signaled a further hike in January. SEB reads this as another attack on Chairman Warsh's reluctance to give forward guidance.
SEB expects a Fed hike in December, with the possibility of another step in March 2027. Data since the October meeting has been strong and Fed members sound increasingly hawkish.
The dollar trades below 1.10 against the euro. Weak Australian labor market data pressured AUD on expectations that the RBA is done hiking, which is also SEB's view.

Musk told the New York Times he is not MAGA and regrets investing about 400 million USD in the Republicans ahead of the Texas election. SEB asks whether this is the first of several outstretched hands from US tech companies now that the balance of power has shifted.

Trump met Putin one-on-one at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen ahead of a tripartite meeting with Xi, and will meet Xi separately later today. Trump said he would not make a deal with Putin about Ukraine without Ukraine's participation.

The Riksbank's executive board is questioned in the Swedish Riksdag Finance Committee today. SEB is watching for clues on the timing of the next hike and how board members weigh inflation risk against the risk of the recovery stalling.
Today's data calendar is thin. It includes Norges Bank's survey of inflation expectations, Eurozone labour costs and construction, and the US Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Markets price a continued Fed tightening cycle. Hawkish minutes and Waller's 50 basis point call support this pricing.

macro_indicators.reading: Hike in December, possible further step in March 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: SEB expects further Fed tightening, with a risk of a larger 50 basis point December move.
Weak Australian labor market data has pressured AUD on expectations that RBA tightening is over, which SEB shares.

risk_factors: Possible US and Israeli attacks on Iran could disturb oil prices, which are at 92 USD/barrel.
Unfavorable inflation data could lead the Fed to hike by 50 basis points instead of 25.
Renewed declines in Nvidia and a five-day S&P 500 losing streak point to fragile sentiment toward AI stocks.
geopolitical: New York Times reports that President Trump is considering new attacks on Iran together with Israel.
APEC meeting in Shenzhen with a historic Trump, Xi and Putin meeting, including one-on-one sessions between Trump and each of the two.
Trump says he will not make a deal with Putin about Ukraine without Ukraine's participation.
